newsitem.title: KENYA: Daring Kenya robbers raid Nairobi petrol station.
newsitem.headline: Daring Kenya robbers raid Nairobi petrol station.

text.p: Gunmen in police uniform robbed a Nairobi petrol station, stealing 694,000 Kenyan shillings ($9,800) and boldly selling petrol for an hour, witnesses said on Tuesday.
About 10 robbers with rifles struck at Vic Preston Junior's petrol station in Nairobi city centre at 3 a.m. on Monday, locking up pump attendants and a security guard and cutting into safes.
Five of them served unsuspecting early morning customers for an hour while the others cracked the safes, witnesses said.
"To any customer coming in for fuel, it was a perfectly normal petrol station, nothing suspicious," said Chris Cooper, the owner's grandson and a supervisor at the station.
The robbers wearing police uniforms and armed with G-3 rifles left behind a police beret as they fled. The G-3 is the standard service rifle for the Kenyan police and armed forces.
Owner Preston, a former rally driver, did not think even the abandoned beret would result in police finding any suspects.
"Have the police ever established anything in this country? To them this is just another robbery," he told Reuters. The petrol station is only about 100 metres (yards) from a police station.
Police spokesman Assistant Commissioner Peter Kimanthi said police were investigating and it was too early to comment.
Some police have taken part in robberies in Kenya and others are widely suspected of hiring out uniforms and weapons to robbers. Police commanders have vowed to stamp out corruption in the force.
